title: Rani Mukerji becomes second Indian film personality after Shah Rukh Khan to receive La Trobe Honorary Doctorate
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:
The star is recognised for her nearly three-decade journey in cinema and her contribution to humanitarian causes.

Adding to this, The recognition comes in honour of Mukerji’s nearly three decades in Indian cinema, as well as her contribution to humanitarian work. Known for taking on characters and stories that have addressed social issues, women’s empowerment and important conversations, the star has consistently used her platform to highlight narratives that resonate beyond entertainment.

Meanwhile, Speaking about the honour, Rani Mukerji shared, “Receiving this honorary doctorate from La Trobe University is one of the most humbling moments of my life,” Mukerji shared. “For someone who has always believed that films can change hearts before they change minds, this recognition means more than I can possibly express.”

Notably, Over the course of her career, Mukerji has featured in films spanning several genres while also choosing projects driven by strong themes and characters. Reflecting on the philosophy behind her choices, she shared, “I have always chosen films that have made an impact in my heart first. A story that needs to be told. A story that would inspire and empower.”

As per the latest buzz, The star also spoke about the larger responsibility that comes with being an artist, particularly when representing Indian cinema and culture on a global platform. “Every artist carries a responsibility beyond performance. We quietly become ambassadors of our culture,” she added.

In further updates, Mukerji further reflected on the impact her work can have on audiences and how films can shape perceptions about India and its women. She went on to continue, “If my films have helped even one person understand India and its women a little better… then I feel I have fulfilled a responsibility far greater than simply being an star.”

On top of that, The honour also places Rani Mukerji in an exclusive league at La Trobe University. Shah Rukh Khan was conferred an honorary doctorate by the university in 2019, and the institution subsequently revealed a PhD scholarship in his name.

With the latest recognition, Mukerji’s contribution to Indian cinema is being acknowledged not only for her performances but also for the cultural and social impact of the stories she has chosen throughout her career.

title: EXCLUSIVE: Scam 1992 writer Sumit Purohit to co-direct Scam 2010 with Hansal Mehta; shooting underway
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Bollywood Hungama has exclusively learned that Sumit Purohit will co-direct Scam 2010 with Hansal Mehta. Purohit was among the writers of the first season and is intimately familiar with the franchise’s tone and storytelling approach, making him a natural fit for the job. The screenwriter made his directorial debut with the espionage thriller series Saare Jahan Se Accha and has also directed the satirical comedy-drama Baaghi Bechare, starring Pratik Gandhi, Abhishek Banerjee and Faisal Malik, which is yet to be rolled out. Scam 2010 will mark a significant step forward for Purohit as he transitions from writer on the first season to co-director of the third instalment.

Adding to this, Scam 2010 delves into the financial scandals surrounding maverick businessman Subrata Roy of Sahara India Pariwar. Marathi star Siddharth Bodke (Devmanus, Drishyam 2) essays the role of Roy, while Kritika Singh (Rangbaaz), Moon Banerjee and CID fame Aditya Srivastava round out the principal cast. The show went on floors in late May and has since been shot across multiple locations, including Lucknow, Kanpur, Delhi, Mumbai and Dehradun. The series is expected to wrap production by mid-September, with a global premiere on SonyLIV targeted for early 2027.

Meanwhile, Produced by Applause Entertainment and Birla Studios, Scam 2010 will chronicle the meteoric rise of Roy’s vast business empire and the prolonged legal battles that followed. Based on Tamal Bandyopadhyay’s 2014 book Sahara: The Untold Story, the new season will explore the contradictions in Roy’s public image while examining the complex intersections of markets, governance and accountability in modern Indian finance.

title: 'Between me and students': CJI Surya Kant slams Bar Council move against protesters
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant on Friday came down heavily on the Bar Council of India (BCI) over its intervention in the NALSAR University of Law enrolment row, saying the Council had “no business” interfering with students’ right to protest and making it clear that the court would not allow students to be stopped from raising their voice through lawful and peaceful protests. He restrained the BCI and all state bar councils from pursuing any punitive or criminal action against students and faculty of any national law university or university in connection with the row.

Adding to this, Chief Justice of India Surya Kant shared, "It's a dialogue between the students and me." (PTI) The CJI’s observations came hours after BCI chairman Manan Kumar Mishra opened up that the Council had decided to close its proceedings against the 2026 graduating batch of NALSAR, Hyderabad, after initially freezing their enrolment and then withdrawing the freeze while retaining an inquiry into those allegedly instrumental in the students’ campaign against CJI Kant being invited as chief guest at their convocation.

Meanwhile, The Supreme Court , meanwhile, took on board a petition seeking directions to restrain the BCI from issuing such directives in future and issued notice to the Council. A bench headed by CJI Kant, along with justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, directed the BCI to file its counter-affidavit within two weeks.

Notably, “The BCI is unnecessarily taking action in this matter. If students have a cause or a reason to protest, they have a right to protest. Nobody can stop them, and we will not allow this,” shared the CJI after senior advocate K Parameshwar mentioned the matter before the bench.

As per the latest buzz, Parameshwar submitted that the BCI had “no business” dealing with what was happening inside a university and that its action violated the students’ fundamental right to freedom of speech and expression. He shared the BCI’s withdrawal of the first letter freezing enrolment did not wipe out the cause of action against the Council. “It spells a lot about the functioning of the BCI,” Parameshwar shared.

In further updates, The CJI responded: “We are with you. This is absolutely uncalled for. They had no business to interfere. The students have written a letter to me, and it is between me and the students. There is a dialogue between us.”

On top of that, The Chief Justice also drew upon his own experience as a student to underscore the importance of allowing dissent on university campuses. “In my younger days, I was also actively involved in student activities. They have a right to protest. Who can stop them? So long as they are lawfully and peacefully protesting, they have a right to raise their voice,” he shared.
At another point, the CJI shared: “We have to be large-hearted. They should be allowed to speak. Even if they are wrong, they have a right to speak.”

title: Awarapan 2 vs Batwara 1947 LIVE Updates: Emraan Hashmi set for his biggest opening, Sunny Deol's Partition drama lags
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Awarapan 2 vs Batwara 1947 live updates: Awarapan 2 stars Emraan Hashmi, while Batwara 1947 is led by Sunny Deol. Awarapan 2 vs Batwara 1947 LIVE Updates: Emraan Hashmi 's Awarapan 2 and Sunny Deol -led Batwara 1947 are vying for the audience's attention in the theatres this Independence Day weekend. Both films have rolled out in theatres on August 14. ...Read More

Adding to this, • Awarapan 2 brings back Emraan Hashmi in his iconic role of Shivam Pandit. The movie also stars Shabana Azmi, Disha Patani, and Suvinder Vicky • Directed by Nitin Kakkar and produced by Vishesh Bhatt, Awarapan 2 resurrects Emraan's character, who had died at the end of the first part. • On the other hand, Batwara 1947 stars Sunny Deol, Shabana Azmi, Preity Zinta, Karan Deol, Ali Fazal, Abhimanyu Singh, Khushi Hajare, and Kanikka Kapur. • Directed by Rajkumar Santoshi, the movie is about a Muslim man who moves to Pakistan during Partition, only to find a Hindu woman still living in his new home. As tensions rise, he takes responsibility for protecting her while keeping his family safe. • Batwara 1947 is based on Asghar Wajahat's bestselling book Jis Lahore Nai Dekhya O Jamyai Nai. • Both films arrive in theatres with substantial hype. Awarapan 2 is a legacy sequel to a cult classic while Batwara 1947 sees the reunion of Sunny and Santoshi's smash hit jodi. • The advance bookings for both films opened 48 hours before rollout. Awarapan 2 scored big, minting over ₹ 8 crore rupees in pre-sales for day 1 alone. • Batwara 1947's advance bookings weren't as manic. The movie managed sales of ₹ 1.76 crore rupees for the opening day.
Meanwhile, On ticketing platform BookMyShow, Awarapan 2 saw a huge surge in sales on Friday morning, with the pace reaching 20k tickets per hour by noon.

Notably, Giving the movie four stars in his review of Awarapan 2 on X, trade analyst Taran Adarsh wrote, “#EmraanHashmi returns as #ShivamPandit, and what a return it is... He is the SOUL of #Awarapan2... Mass-appealing moments + tremendous nostalgia value... SURE-SHOT SUCCESS.”

As per the latest buzz, Talking to reporters last week, Sunny Deol shared, “When you see the movie, you will forget what it is. You will be so involved in the cinema that you will come out happy and satisfied. It will make you realise what the Partition was. And how important it is to stand by yourself against all the odds.”

In further updates, Batwara 1947 director Santoshi shared that the crux of the story is human courage and will, not the divide between people. “This is an emotional story. What will stay with you are the characters. The story doesn’t see Hindu or Muslim. The characters see human beings. Ek insaan ke saath ek ghatna hoti hai aur insaan kis tarah se kya karta hai (Something occurs with a human being and how other human beings rally together), that is the story. Toh ek message nahi de raha hoon main. Teacher thode hi hoon (I am not giving a message, I am not a teacher). The movie should be good, and people should enjoy it,” he shared.

On top of that, Filmmaker Ramesh Taurani watched Batwara 1947 at a special screening on Wednesday and wrote on Instagram, “Batwara 1947 is a deeply sensitive, moving and truly humanity-glorifying movie that deserves to be watched First Day, First Show. It is a powerful reminder of the resilience of the human spirit and the importance of compassion, especially during the darkest chapters of our history. @iamsunnydeol delivers a terrific and deeply impactful performance. And what a joy it is to see @realpz doing what she does best on the big screen. @azmishabana18, @alifazal9 and @imkarandeol are all exceptional in their respective roles, bringing such depth, intensity and authenticity to the movie. @abhimanyusingh.44 is terrific as the villain, creating a character that is both compelling and deeply unsettling.”
According to Sacnilk, the Sunny Deol movie sold 65k tickets for its opening day, grossing ₹ 1.76 crore rupees in advance bookings.

title: Kitu Gidwani calls Bollywood ‘fake industry’, slams its vague rules: ‘I should have been able to live off royalties’
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Star Kitu Gidwani has spent over four decades in the entertainment industry, working across films and television and building a career that includes memorable projects such as Jaane Tu Ya Jaane Na , Fashion and Dhobi Ghat, as well as iconic TV shows like Shaktimaan and Swabhimaan. Now, the veteran star has opened up about some of her biggest frustrations with Bollywood, calling the industry "fake" and questioning its treatment of artistes, particularly older women. In a recent interview with Screen, Kitu also criticised the lack of royalties for artistes and the limited, stereotypical roles offered to women as they age.

Adding to this, Kitu Gidwani slams lack of powerful roles for women in Bollywood. Kitu Gidwani slams Bollywood Talking about how several musicians have been fighting for unpaid royalties, Kitu shared actors face the same issue. She shared, "Bollywood is not a real industry; it’s a cottage industry. It’s a fake industry; it goes by its own vague rules. There is nothing like Hollywood’s Screen Actors Guild in India. I should have been able to work for 10 years and then live off my royalties for the next ten years, not slog for 40 years. Intellectual property rights and creative rights are zero in India."

Meanwhile, She further criticised the lack of rights actors have over their work, pointing out that producers typically pay actors and directors a one-time fee and then retain complete ownership and control over the property. She added, "It’s not like that anywhere in the world. My grouse against the industry is that older women are not getting powerful roles. We don’t want to play the generic mother or maasi. We want to play good, enduring roles with sex, love, power, comedy, and action. In daily soaps, once a woman hits 30, she becomes a daadi. She has no signs of aging on her face, but she gets such roles. This industry is very bizarre.”

Notably, In Hollywood, actors are represented by unions such as SAG-AFTRA, while writers and directors have the WGA and DGA, respectively. These unions have negotiated provisions that can provide performers and writers with additional payments when films, television shows or other content are reused, syndicated, licensed or made available on certain platforms. These payments are often referred to as residuals.

As per the latest buzz, Kitu began her acting journey in 1984 with the movie Holi, which also featured Aamir Khan, Ashutosh Gowariker, Om Puri and others. She gained popularity after starring in the TV series Air Hostess, which aired on Doordarshan in 1986. She then played Svetlana in Swabhimaan, which made her a household name. She later joined Shaktimaan, playing Geeta Vishwas, a news reporter who stood for the truth. However, she left the show after a few episodes.

In further updates, Apart from television, Kitu has also received critical acclaim for her performances in films such as Dance of the Wind (1997), Deepa Mehta's Earth (1998), Govind Nihalani's Rukhmavati Ki Haveli (1991), Kamal Haasan's Abhay and Deham (2001).

title: Rani Mukerji honoured for 3 decades in cinema: ‘My films, my characters and my voice have travelled so far from home’
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Rani Mukerji has added another major honour to her three-decade-long career. The star was recognised at the Indian Movie Festival of Melbourne (IFFM) with a special citation for excellence in acting, celebrating her memorable performances and the lasting impact she has had on audiences in India and around the world. The honour acknowledges Rani's contribution to Indian cinema and her role in taking stories and characters from Hindi films to global audiences.

Adding to this, Rani Mukerji honoured for three decades of cinema: ‘They've made me a better star’. Rani Mukerji celebrates 3 decades of roles Rani attended the festival in a striking geranium-red monochrome co-ord set as she marked the latest recognition in an already celebrated career. From playing women who went against social expectations to portraying characters who found courage during difficult times, the star has consistently brought honesty and emotional depth to her performances.

Meanwhile, Her filmography includes a wide range of roles, with films such as Black, Hum Tum, Yuva, Bunty Aur Babli, No One Killed Jessica, Hichki, the Mardaani franchise and Mrs. Chatterjee vs Norway showcasing different sides of her acting.

Notably, Speaking about the honour, Rani Mukerji shared, “When I entered the Indian movie industry as a young girl, I never imagined that one day my films and the characters that I have been fortunate enough to play would take me across oceans, and that people in a beautiful country like Australia would embrace me with so much warmth. Entertaining people across the world through my cinema is the greatest gift this profession has given me. Australia has always welcomed me and Indian cinema with open arms. It has become a place where cultures meet through storytelling, where films remind us that emotions don't need passports, and where love, laughter and hope speak a language we all understand.”

As per the latest buzz, She also reflected on how her characters have shaped her personally over the years. Rani added, “As actors, we perform in front of a camera. But the real story begins only when that performance reaches someone's heart. To know that for three decades my films, my characters and my voice have travelled so far from home and still found a place in your lives is incredibly humbling. I've been fortunate to play women who laughed loudly, loved deeply, fought fearlessly and never stopped believing in themselves. In many ways, every character has changed me a little. They've made me a better star, but more importantly, they've made me a better human being.”

In further updates, Rani's recognition also highlights the growing international reach of Indian cinema and her long-standing connection with audiences outside India. Her work has travelled well beyond the traditional Hindi movie audience, with several of her performances continuing to resonate with viewers across different cultures.
On top of that, The 2026 edition of IFFM is being held from August 13 to 23 and brings together films, actors and filmmakers from across India.

title: Sunny Deol recreates 'papa hu papa' from Oggy and the Cockroaches to perfection, internet can't believe the crossover
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Star Sunny Deol has been busy promoting his new movie, Batwara 1947. For the same, the veteran star undertook a massive nationwide city tour along with the movie’s cast and director Rajkumar Santoshi . One of the final stops in the tour was Kolkata, where he interacted with followers at an event. But apart from some Batwara talks, Sunny stunned followers with a rather unbelievable crossover. The star obliged a fan, recreating a dialogue from the animated show Oggy and the Cockroaches, which was dubbed in ‘his voice’ originally.

Adding to this, Sunny Deol channeled his inner Jack during the movie promotion of Batwara 1947, in Kolkata on Wednesday. (ANI Photo) Sunny Deol’s Oggy and the Cockroaches shoutout In videos shared from the stage at the Kolkata event for Batwara 1947, Sunny addresses a large, packed auditorium when a fan asks him to say a line. Explaining the context, the fan tells the star about Oggy and the Cockroaches. “There is a line in it in your voice, sir, where the character says, ‘Oye main papa hoon, duniya ka papa (I am the daddy, world’s daddy). Please can you say that in your style.”

Meanwhile, Sunny first smiles at the request and says, “I haven’t watched it, but you are saying he says, ‘main papa hoon, duniya ka papa’. So let me try.” The star then recreated the line in Hindi and Punjabi in his signature bold style to loud cheers from the crowd.
Notably, View this post on Instagram A post shared by Samagya (@samagya_entertainment)

As per the latest buzz, The video of Sunny giving Oggy and the Cockroaches a shoutout in this manner went widely shared on Instagram in no time. Many comments expressed disbelief. “Now I can die peacefully,” chirped one. Another shared, “We got Sunny paaji saying Jack’s line before GTA VI.” Others took it further and joked that this style would look funny for Sunny’s next character. The star plays Lord Hanuman in Ramayana. “Imagine him saying to Ravana-Oye utha utha k patkunga tod dunga fod dunga oye..main papa hun iss Lanka ka Papa,” joked one social media user.

In further updates, Oggy and the Cockroaches was an animated series created in Canada by Jean-Yves Raimbaud and produced by Gaumont Multimedia. It aired from 1998 to 2019 across seven seasons. It began airing on Nickelodeon in India in 2009. In 2012, it was acquired by Cartoon Network for India, acquiring Bollywood-style voiceovers, with Jack, a green cat, voiced in the style of Sunny Deol. The series and its voice acting proved extremely popular in India, making the show part of the country's pop culture.

On top of that, Helmed by Rajkumar Santoshi, the movie stars Sunny Deol as a Muslim man who moves to Pakistan during Partition, only to find a Hindu woman, played by Shabana Azmi, still living in his new home. As tensions rise, he takes responsibility for protecting her while keeping his family safe. The movie also stars Preity Zinta, Karan Deol, Ali Fazal, Abhimanyu Singh, Khushi Hajare, and Kanikka Kapur. Backed by Aamir Khan Productions, the movie has rolled out in theatres today (August 14).

title: Pooja Bedi says she won't marry fiancé Maneck Contractor despite 8-year engagement: 'I've been there, done that'
body: Here's the latest relationship update doing the rounds:

Star Pooja Bedi has opened up about her decision not to marry her fiancé Maneck Contractor , despite the couple having been engaged for eight years. In a recent conversation with Vickey Lalwani on his YouTube channel, Pooja explained how her views on marriage have changed over the years and why she no longer sees the need to formalise their relationship.

Adding to this, Pooja Bedi is engaged to Maneck Contractor. Pooja Bedi reveals why she doesn't want to get married Pooja opened up that while she once strongly believed in the institution of marriage, her views have evolved over the years. She shared that she is currently in a relationship with Maneck and that they have been engaged for eight years. While people often ask them when they plan to get married, she reminds them that they are not getting married.

Meanwhile, Explaining her decision not to marry, Pooja shared, "Engagement is when a person puts a ring on your finger and says, 'I want to be married to you.' Which basically says, I want to spend the rest of my life with you by my side, as a companion, as your lover, as your husband, and as a father of your children. The commitment is enough. After the commitment is there, all you're really doing is signing a piece of paper and getting the government involved in your affair.”

Notably, "It is so much easier. I've been married, I've been divorced, and I have two children. He's been married, he's been divorced, and he has kids too. In terms of simple things, like in terms of your assets, it's so simple. My assets go to my kids; his assets go to his kids. I'm earning, he's earning, and we're both independent. I don't need him for security's sake. He doesn't need me for financial security,” she added.

As per the latest buzz, Pooja shared that while the intention was initially to get married, the reality of what marriage looked like for them did not align with their vision for life. She explained that she does not want to be "contracted to somebody", adding that she has "been there, done that". She shared she believes everyone should get married and considers marriage a wonderful space, but does not personally feel the need to do it again.

In further updates, Pooja Bedi is the daughter of star Kabir Bedi and the late classical dancer Protima Bedi. She married businessman Farhan Furniturewala in 1994 and stepped away from films after marriage. The couple welcomed two children, daughter Alaya F and son Omar, before ending their marriage in 2003. Bedi has maintained a cordial relationship with Farhan, who is now married to Laila Khan Furniturewala.

On top of that, A few years after her divorce, Pooja reconnected with Maneck, who had been her senior at The Lawrence School, Sanawar, through their alumni WhatsApp group. In 2019, he proposed to her atop a hot-air balloon. Announcing her engagement, she tweeted, “He has literally swept me off my feet... i accepted Maneck Contractor’s proposal whilst sailing in a hot air balloon. Wish all of you a lifetime of happiness & to always dream of a rainbow at the end of a storm.”

title: Cocktail 2 OTT release: When and where to watch Shahid Kapoor, Kriti Sanon, Rashmika Mandanna's ₹147 crore hit
body: Here's the latest box office buzz making the rounds:

Almost two months after its theatrical rollout, romantic drama Cocktail 2, starring Shahid Kapoor , Kriti Sanon, and Rashmika Mandanna , is set to rollout on streaming. The movie received criticism upon rollout but was eventually a box-office success.

Adding to this, Cocktail 2 OTT rollout: Shahid Kapoor, Kriti Sanon, Rashmika movie is now out on streaming. Cocktail 2 OTT rollout Starting Friday, August 14, Cocktail 2 will begin streaming on Netflix. Sharing the update on social media, a post on the streaming giant's account read, “Two's a couple, and three's a Cocktail You've got a date Watch Cocktail 2, out 14 August on Netflix .” This was accompanied by a poster of the movie.
Meanwhile, View this post on Instagram A post shared by Netflix India (@netflix_in)

Notably, Directed by Homi Adjania, Cocktail 2 follows Shahid Kapoor and Rashmika Mandanna, a young couple deeply in love but unsure about marriage. Their vacation in Sicily takes an unexpected turn when they meet Diya's friend Ally, played by Kriti Sanon . What begins as a carefree trip soon turns into an emotional test of trust, love, and commitment.

As per the latest buzz, Cocktail 2 rolled out in theatres on June 19, 2026 to largely negative reviews. On the review aggregator website Rotten Tomatoes, only 23% of the movie's reviews are positive. It has a weighted rating of 5 out of 10 on the platform. Cocktail 2 was criticised for its lack of depth, slow pace, and not enough layers in the female characters. The HT review of the movie read: “This spiritual successor has the gloss, the glamour, but not the emotional punch. Some drinks are best served once.”

In further updates, Despite this, the movie was a big box-office success. The movie opened at ₹ 13 crore rupees net in India and sprinted to ₹ 47 crore rupees domestically in its opening weekend. Even as word of mouth did not pick up as expected, Cocktail 2 was able to cross ₹ 100 crore rupees domestically, on top of $3.7 million overseas. By the end of its run in theatres last week, Cocktail 2 had collected ₹ 147 crore rupees worldwide. As of August 14, it is the 6th-highest-grossing Hindi movie of the year.

On top of that, Cocktail 2 is the spiritual successor to director Homi Adajania's Cocktail, a critical and commercial success rolled out in 2012. The original movie starred Deepika Padukone, Saif Ali Khan, and Diana Penty.

title: Batwara 1947 and Awarapan 2 Movie Review, Release Live Updates
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

SUMMARY Emraan Hashmi returns to one of his most recognisable characters with 'Awarapan 2', which hits theatres today, almost two decades after the first movie. Directed by Nitin Kakkar, the sequel brings back Hashmi as Shivam, with Disha Patani and Shabana Azmi joining him in key roles. The biggest advantage for the movie is undoubtedly the emotional connect that the 2007 original has developed over the years. While 'Awarapan' did not emerge as a major theatrical success upon rollout, its music, intense romantic drama and Hashmi's portrayal of a troubled gangster gradually collected it a loyal cult following. The sequel appears to be consciously tapping into that sentiment, bringing back the character and the world that followers have remained attached to. The music is another major nostalgia factor, with the soundtrack carrying the musical identity associated with the franchise and a reprise of the much-loved 'Toh Phir Aao' adding to the recall value. For Hashmi, who has experienced several ups and downs at the ticket-window in recent years, the movie could provide a much-needed commercial breakthrough. A strong opening combined with positive word of mouth could make 'Awarapan 2' one of his most significant successes in a long time. Running alongside it is Sunny Deol's 'Batwara 1947', a period drama directed by Rajkumar Santoshi and produced by Aamir Khan. The movie features an ensemble cast comprising Deol, Preity Zinta, Shabana Azmi, Karan Deol, Ali Fazal and Abhimanyu Singh. Set around the Partition of India, the story examines the human cost of one of the most traumatic chapters in the subcontinent's history. Deol plays Sikander Mirza, while Zinta portrays Hamida Mirza and Azmi takes on the role of Mai. The narrative revolves around a Muslim family that moves into a house in Lahore after Partition, only to encounter the Hindu woman who remains connected to the property, bringing questions of displacement, identity, loss and humanity to the forefront. The movie also reunites Santoshi and Deol while bringing Deol and Zinta back together on screen, adding another layer of nostalgia. Interestingly, Shabana Azmi is the common link between the two Hindi releases, appearing in pivotal roles in both films. The two Bollywood releases, however, have another major challenge to contend with: Marvel's 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day', which has already been playing in Indian cinemas since July 30. Starring Tom Holland, Zendaya, Jacob Batalon, Jon Bernthal and Mark Ruffalo, the superhero movie has established a strong theatrical presence before the arrival of the two new Hindi films. With the Hollywood smash hit already commanding screens and audience attention, 'Awarapan 2' and 'Batwara 1947' will have to carve out their own space through their respective strengths – nostalgia and music on one side and star power, emotion and historical drama on the other. The Independence Day weekend therefore sets up an intriguing three-way box-office battle. Live Events 10:05 (IST) Aug 14 Batwara 1947 movie review: Strong word of mouth The initial reactions suggest that 'Batwara 1947' could benefit from positive word of mouth. The movie has received praise from viewers who watched morning shows.
Adding to this, The reported reactions indicate that Sunny Deol's performance remains one of the movie's biggest attractions. The movie's message of communal harmony has also been appreciated.
Meanwhile, Shabana Azmi is another key performer in the two-movie ticket-window conversation. She plays an important role in 'Batwara 1947' and has been lauded by early viewers.

Notably, The movie's emotional approach appears to have connected with audiences. Sunny Deol's character and the movie's focus on humanity have also emerged as recurring points in the early reactions.
As per the latest buzz, The story's central character continues to be Shivam Pandit. The reviewers lauded the writers for keeping his journey at the heart of the sequel.

In further updates, X review shared, "Writers #BilalSiddiqui and #VisheshBhatt ensure that the backbone of the story – #ShivamPandit – remains the focal point... The writers also know when to hold back and when to hit hard, resulting in several sequences that genuinely stay with you."
On top of that, The review also highlighted how the sequel uses moments from the first movie. These references are shared to strengthen the connection between the two films.

It added, "Additionally, he smartly incorporates flashes from the first part, leveraging the recall value and nostalgia factor... These moments seamlessly connect the two films while giving followers a sense of familiarity."

title: Shah Rukh Khan becomes Foxtale’s new brand ambassador; to represent serum, sunscreen and more
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

The partnership marks a new phase for Foxtale, which was launched four years ago and has since built a consumer community of more than 10 million people. The brand positions itself around science-backed skincare formulated with Indian skin and climate in mind.

Adding to this, With ‘Let Your Glow Through’, Foxtale aims to expand its messaging beyond individual skincare products. According to the brand, its formulations are developed by focusing on the source of skin concerns rather than relying only on surface-level solutions.

Meanwhile, The philosophy also reflects the brand’s view that skincare should not be about constantly adding more products or trying to change one’s appearance. Instead, Foxtale believes skincare should help consumers care for and bring out what they already have.

Notably, The brand shared Shah Rukh Khan was chosen as its ambassador because his public image and career align with the values behind the new philosophy. Foxtale highlighted qualities such as confidence, authenticity and substance, which it believes have remained central to the star’s appeal over the years.

As per the latest buzz, Speaking about the announcement, Romita Mazumdar, Founder and CEO of Foxtale, shared, “Everything we've built at Foxtale has started with one belief: that lasting results come from understanding the source, not simply treating the surface. 'Let Your Glow Through' is an extension of that belief. And it will continue to be the philosophy that will guide everything going forward.”

In further updates, She added, “Shah Rukh Khan felt like a natural partner because he represents the same idea. Across decades, what people have connected with has never just been what they see, but who he is. We're delighted to have him join us as we take Foxtale into its next chapter.”

On top of that, Foxtale currently operates across skincare, body care, lip care and fragrance categories. The company says its products are developed using consumer insights and science, with a focus on the needs of Indian consumers.
With Khan joining the brand and the introduction of its new philosophy, Foxtale is looking to build its next phase around the idea of skincare that works “from the source, through the surface”.

title: Collective Studios' Historyverse announces original series on Bhagat Singh
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

The series will move beyond the widely known chapters of Bhagat Singh's life to explore the person behind the icon; his childhood, formative experiences, intellectual influences and the social and political environment that shaped his worldview. It will trace the evolution of these experiences and ideas through the different chapters of his life, culminating in the revolutionary figure whose legacy continues to endure. Set against the backdrop of a changing India in the early 20th century, the story will examine how Bhagat Singh's ideas and convictions evolved to ultimately define his legacy.

Adding to this, For Manish Hathiramani, the project marks his debut as a producer and reflects a personal interest in exploring the lesser-known dimensions of India's history through historically rooted entertainment.

Meanwhile, Speaking about the project, Sudeep Lahiri, Head of Channels and Distribution at Collective Media Network, shared, “There are some figures in our history whose stories we think we know completely. Bhagat Singh is one of them. But behind the icon was a young man whose ideas, influences and experiences shaped the person he would become. That is the story we are interested in exploring. Having Manish come on board as a co-producer makes this collaboration particularly exciting, because we share a strong belief in finding new perspectives within stories that have already been told many times and bringing them to audiences with scale and ambition.”

Notably, Manish Hathiramani, Investor and Entrepreneur, shared, “Bhagat Singh is a figure whose life has always fascinated me, but what interests me most is the person before the legend. We know the revolutionary, the freedom fighter and the icon; this series gives us an opportunity to understand the many facets of Bhagat Singh's life and the journey that shaped him. I am delighted to be producing this project with Historyverse and to bring a fresh perspective on his life and legacy to audiences.”

As per the latest buzz, The series is currently in development, with its title, cast and further details to be revealed at a later date. The project joins Historyverse's expanding slate of Indian history and culturally rooted storytelling, which seeks to revisit significant figures, stories and traditions through contemporary formats and ambitious new approaches to storytelling.

title: Kangana Ranaut defends calling Naseeruddin Shah ‘lomdi’; says, “Whenever you look at his films, interviews or statements, it is always about Pakistan”
body: Here's the latest fashion moment turning heads:

Reiterating her position, Kangana as per reports told ANI, “I shared this about Naseeruddin Shah because he had made such a distasteful video in which he was making threats of this kind. And whenever you look at his films, interviews or statements, it is always about Pakistan. Yeh Pakistan ki prem katha kab khatam hogi? Jab dekho Pakistan ke prem mein yeh mare rahte hain. Ab Partition ko bhi itne saal ho gaye hain toh yeh love story khatam kyun nahi ho rahi hai (When will this love story with Pakistan end? They are always lost in love for Pakistan. It has been so many years since the Partition, when will they end this love story?)

Adding to this, The star turned politician also recalled the protests she experienced personally and claimed that demonstrators had gathered outside her residence. Describing the situation, she shared, “People even climbed up to the gate of my house; there were at least two and a half thousand people outside, and such a massive police force had to be deployed that we couldn't sleep at night.” She added, “So when a situation like this was unfolding at Jantar Mantar, they were all shedding crocodile tears.”

Meanwhile, Kangana further questioned Bollywood’s response to protests involving young people, drawing a comparison with the ongoing situation in Jharkhand. Taking aim at what she considers selective solidarity within the industry, she went on to say, “But now that children in Jharkhand are facing this kind of oppression, aren’t they Gen Z too? Is someone only considered Gen Z if they act against the country or abuse the Prime Minister? They themselves have been made to appear anti-youth. This hypocrisy in the movie industry will not work. The crocodile tears that people from the movie industry were shedding for Jantar Mantar, they should shed the same tears for the children in Jharkhand as well.”

Notably, Speaking about her earlier remark directed towards Naseeruddin Shah, Kangana had shared, “Sach toh yeh hai har koi kisi na kisi ka kutta hai, lekin mujhe iss baat ka garv hai ki main jis ghar (desh) ki roti khati hoon uski rakhwali karti hoon/uske liye ladti hoon, Nasir Saab khaate toh iss desh ka hain lekin ladte padose desh keliye hain. (The truth is, everyone is someone's dog; but I take pride in the fact that I guard--and fight for--the household (country) whose bread I eat. Nasir Saab, on the other hand, eats this country's bread but fights for the neighboring country).”

As per the latest buzz, She then addressed her use of the term “lomdi”, making it clear that she stood by the remark. Kangana shared, “PS In today's time it's a compliment for humans to be called a dog because loyalty and cuteness are so rare. I'd rather be a dog than a lomdi like Nasiruddin.”

In further updates, Kangana’s latest comments come as she continues to voice her opinions on political and social issues, while her remarks about Naseeruddin Shah remain part of the larger conversation around differing viewpoints within the Indian movie industry.

title: Aaradhya Bachchan case: Delhi High Court asks if Bachchan family reputation extends across generations
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Justice Anup Jairam Bhambhani raised the issue during the hearing while discussing the legal protection attached to a person's reputation. The judge questioned whether the reputation associated with a prominent family name could be compared with the goodwill attached to a trademark and, if so, how far such protection could extend.

Adding to this, “The value of trademark and reputation in the trademark arises from the fact that a product or service has been rendered. Now, this is somewhat contextually different when you are talking about a person. A certain last name has a reputation because of the achievements, the eminence in a certain field of work, etc. So, does that reputation, you are couching it as virtually as a trademark, does that flow down generationally? If so, up to what point?” Justice Bhambhani remarked.

Meanwhile, The Court subsequently framed three broad questions that it will consider in the matter. It asked whether a family name, when associated with a reputation similar to that of a trademark, can retain that reputation across generations and, if so, to what extent.

Notably, The Court will also examine whether fake news, even when it is “of egregiously despicable nature”, can constitute an intellectual property rights violation and, if it does, what specific category of intellectual property rights may be involved.

As per the latest buzz, Another question concerns the relationship between defamation and intellectual property law. The Court will consider whether the legal concepts of slander, libel or other forms of injury to reputation can be treated as intellectual property rights.
In further updates, “These are the general questions in my mind. This is not exhaustive,” the Court clarified.

On top of that, Aaradhya Bachchan, through her father Abhishek Bachchan, approached the Delhi High Court in 2023 against several YouTube channels and unidentified individuals, commonly referred to as John Doe defendants. The suit sought to prevent the publication of content that allegedly tarnished the Bachchan family name, invaded their privacy or made defamatory claims about Aaradhya.

The case specifically referred to multiple YouTube videos that made false claims about Aaradhya’s health. Some videos allegedly claimed that she was seriously unwell and had been admitted to a hospital, while another claimed that the minor had died. The content also allegedly accused her family of failing to provide her with timely medical treatment.

title: EXCLUSIVE: V. Shantaram biopic starring Siddhant Chaturvedi and Tamannaah Bhatia pushed to 2027; director reveals reason for delay
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Speaking exclusively to Bollywood Hungama , the movie's director, Abhijeet Shirish Deshpande, has clarified that the V. Shantaram biopic is very much on track and production has instead been moved to 2027. “We had initially planned an April shoot and planned to go indoors after rains. But we were delayed by two months, and then the whole schedule went haywire. Now with the fresh dates, we are planning to shoot next year with a few more big names in the casting apart from Sidharth and Tamannaah,” the filmmaker revealed.

Adding to this, The makers are now aiming to commence its shooting in April 2027. The revised schedule has been planned in a way that will allow the team to complete outdoor sequences first and then utilize the monsoon period for interior shoots.

Meanwhile, The movie chronicles Shantaram’s remarkable journey from the silent era through the advent of sound and color, showcasing his evolution as one of India’s most influential filmmakers. Shantaram is known for directing memorable films in Hindi and Marathi, including Do Aankhen Barah Haath (1957), Dr. Kotnis Ki Amar Kahani (1946), Amar Bhoopali (1951), and Pinjara (1971).

Notably, The project marks Siddhant Chaturvedi's first biographical role, and he's excited to get into the skin of the visionary filmmaker known for his signature style of lavish sets, unique song picturizations, and visual symbolism. During the announcement, he had called the opportunity one of the greatest honors of his life. “The more I read about his journey, the more humbled I felt. He wasn’t just a pioneer of Indian and global cinema, he was a visionary who kept pushing forward no matter the obstacles,” Chaturvedi shared. “Stepping into his world has been my most transformative experience as an star. His life moved me deeply and reminded me of the power of perseverance. It’s a lesson I hope to hold close, both in my work and in every moment of my life.”

title: Shilpa Shetty, Arjun Kapoor to join Kiran Bedi, Jai Madaan and others at World Happpiness Summit 2026 in Bengaluru
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

The summit will be held at New Horizon College of Engineering against the backdrop of Bengaluru, a city known for technology, innovation, entrepreneurship and professional ambition. The conversations will look at happiness beyond achievements, financial milestones and social status, with sessions around purpose, relationships, inner peace, mental well-being, fulfilment and the pressures that accompany modern success. Shilpa Shetty and Arjun Kapoor will bring perspectives from entertainment and popular culture, while Kiran Bedi, Sonu Sharma, Hema Sardesai, Jai Madaan and Dr. Saamdu Chetri will contribute perspectives from public service, entrepreneurship, music, wellness, spirituality and the philosophy of Gross National Happiness.

Adding to this, At the centre of the summit is Happpy AiR - Atman in Ravi’s belief that true ‘Happpiness’ is a harmonious mix of Pleasure, Peace and Purpose — the three Ps. “We spend so much of our lives preparing to become happpy someday, after the next achievement, the next milestone or the next success. But happiness is not a destination we arrive at. It is something we can experience in the present moment,” he shared. He added that the three Ps form the basis of his understanding of happiness (that’s the reason why he spells happpiness with three Ps) and that the summit is an effort to take this thought beyond an individual philosophy and create a larger conversation around what it means to live a happy and fulfilled life.

Meanwhile, The World Happpiness Summit is part of the larger #Happpy.AiR.Movement, which seeks to create a wider dialogue around happiness, inner peace and purposeful living. The initiative comes at a time when Bengaluru continues to attract entrepreneurs, technology professionals, creators and young talent from across India, and seeks to explore whether a city known for ambition and opportunity can also become a benchmark for happiness and well-being. The World Happpiness Summit 2026 will be held on September 24 at New Horizon College of Engineering, Bengaluru.

title: Awarapan 2 beats part 1's lifetime box office haul with advance bookings alone, Emraan Hashmi film set for massive start
body: Here's the latest box office buzz making the rounds:

It may come as a surprise to many younger readers who keep hearing only positive things about Emraan Hashmi ’s Awarapan from older audiences, but when it rolled out in 2007, the movie was a ticket-window bomb. The ambitious movie from Vishesh Films managed to earn a mere ₹ 7.7 crore rupees net in its lifetime. But over the years, as viewers discovered it on home media, cable, and eventually streaming, Awarapan gained a cult following. That belated credibility and love are now helping the sequel, set to rollout this weekend. Awarapan 2 is tracking to have one of the biggest openings for Bollywood in 2026. In fact, the buzz is so strong that the movie is set to cross part 1’s lifetime earnings even before rollout.

Adding to this, Emraan Hashmi on the promotional poster of Awarapan 2. Awarapan 2 advance bookings The advance bookings for Awarapan 2 began just 48 hours before rollout, but were off to a rollicking start on Wednesday itself. By 3 PM on Thursday, just 18 hours before the movie hits screens, Awarapan 2 has sold over 1.3 lakh tickets for rollout day. According to Sacnilk, the movie has sold tickets worth ₹ 4 crore rupees for its opening day. Trade insiders estimate that total advance bookings for the movie's opening weekend and beyond exceed ₹ 9 crore rupees gross ( ₹ 7-8 crore rupees net). This means that even before rollout, Awarapan 2 has surpassed the lifetime collection of its predecessor.

Meanwhile, Awarapan had an opening-day collection of ₹ 79 lakh and netted ₹ 2.88 crore rupees in its first weekend. Even after accounting for inflation, this was a low figure. In contrast, Awarapan 2 is expected to be Emraan Hashmi’s highest opener, potentially reaching the ₹ 20 crore rupees mark on day 1.

Notably, Awarapan 2 is clashing with Sunny Deol’s Batwara 1947 at the ticket-window. But trade analysts say that Awarapan 2 will be the winner of this battle. Most estimates put the movie’s opening at a staggering ₹ 20 crore rupees net. Even the more conservative estimates are around ₹ 15-18 crore rupees, a solid figure. As things stand, Awarapan 2 should be looking to cross ₹ 100 crore rupees worldwide in its opening weekend itself, eight times part 1’s lifetime collection. That is an extraordinary turnaround.

As per the latest buzz, Directed by Nitin Kakkar and produced by Vishesh Bhatt, Awarapan 2 brings back Emraan Hashmi in his iconic role of Shivam Pandit. The movie also stars Shabana Azmi, Disha Patani , and Suvinder Vicky. Awarapan 2 arrives in theatres on August 14.

In further updates, Abhimanyu Mathur is Deputy Editor, Entertainment at Hindustan Times. With almost 15 years of experience in writing about everything from films and TV shows to cricket matches and elections, he inhales and exhales pop culture and news. Currently, he watches movies and TV shows and talks to celebrities for a living, while occasionally writing about them as well. A journalism graduate of Delhi College of Arts and Commerce, Delhi University, Abhimanyu began his career with Hindustan Times at the age of 20, swapping classrooms for newsrooms at an early age. He began his journey in the early days of digital journalism, later switching to the madness of print journalism. Work has led him to far off places like Japan and Jordan, as well as to the interiors of Haryana and the Indo-Pak border. He dabbled in city reporting in places like Meerut, Gurgaon, and Delhi, covered the Olympics and Cricket World Cups, before finding his calling in entertainment and lifestyle during the pandemic. A Rotten Tomatoes Certified Movie Critic, he is equally at home covering stories on ground as he is interviewing celebrities and studios, and sometimes prefers to shepherd teams in delivering traffic through the day. Even as his role has evolved from reporter to supervisor over the years, his first love remains writing (and of late, talking on camera). title: Kangana Ranaut says half the people at Jantar Mantar protest were of Shabana Azmi's age: ‘Kaise Gen Z protest?’
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Star and BJP MP Kangana Ranaut stirred row after she shared that some young Hindu women flaunt freedom without accountability and called them ‘generation gutter’. After backlash over her comments from the opposition party members, Kangana has now added another clarification.

Adding to this, Kangana Ranaut has further defended her comments on the Gen Z-led protests in Delhi. What Kangana shared On Thursday, Kangana shared a video of herself to defend her statement on Instagram Stories. She added, “Poore desh ke yuva? Agar aap sirf Gen Z ki baat karte hai, toh almost 30-35 crore rupees ke paas inki population hone waali hai. Jo Jantar Mantar hai waha par 10,000 log ekhatta hue the jinme toh aadhey se jyada log toh Shabana Azmi-type log the, aapne dekha ki har type ke age group ghum rahe the. Agar hum yuvaon ki baat karte hain, Gen Z ki hum specifically baat karte hai toh lag bhag waha par 2000 Gen Z the, toh kaise ye log isko Gen Z protest keh rahe hai? Ki poore desh ki Gen Z protest kar rahe (The youth of this country? If we speak of Gen Z, then the population is around 30-35 crore rupees. Around 10,000 people were in Jantar Mantar where more than half of them were Shabana Azmi-type people, so many age group people were present. If we specifically speak of the Gen Z then only 2000 of them were present. So how is it a Gen Z protest? That the entire country's Gen Z were there)?”

Meanwhile, She went on to add, "Ye jo yaha par nasal ikkathha hui thi, usi ke baare mein jo he maine specifically kaha tha. Main aapko open challenge deti hu, mera koi aisa specific quote bataiye jaha maine poori generation ko include kiya ho? Ye faltu ka agenda aap mere saath mat chalaiye! Main yuva-virodhi nahi ho sakti kyuki main khud yuva hoon (It was for the crowd which had gathered outside, I had specifically spoken about them. I am giving an open challenge to pick out any quote where I directed it for the entire generation. Don't throw this useless agenda at me. I am not against the youth because I am one of them)."

Notably, Veteran Bollywood star Shabana Azmi , 75, joined thousands of protestors in their march towards Parliament at Jantar Mantar on July 20. In the photos and videos she posted on Instagram, she was seen travelling in a truck and even crossing barricades alongside the protesters. She had also shared a photo of herself travelling in a truck during the protest march, alongside star Prakash Raj .

As per the latest buzz, Meanwhile, Kangana had earlier criticized the Gen Z protests. "Never in my life have I seen so much ugliness in one place. These reels from Gen Z protests are puke-inducing. The way they speak and the kind of language they are using... never in my life have I seen everything in each and every frame so jarring and so crass all at once....I call them Generation Gutter. Some of them have nothing to offer to the system. They are not good at studies...," she had shared last month.

In further updates, After backlash for her remarks, Kangana had shared she had not made a blanket statement about the protest at Jantar Mantar over the NEET-UG paper leak and she "specifically referred to some people or some women". "Those who call themselves cockroaches, and we say that cockroaches emerge from gutters, what is wrong with that? My point is simply this: if people label themselves as cockroaches, and we say the gutter is their home, why should they be offended? I certainly don't consider myself a cockroach. If someone were to say I live in a gutter, I would deny it. But if someone claims to be a cockroach, then naturally, they would live in a gutter. Where else? But to claim that I was referring to all youth is simply not the case," she told news agency ANI on Wednesday.

title: Bombay HC restrains Sanjay Dutt's Pune nightclub from playing songs without authorisation
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

In an order passed on August 7, the Bombay High Court granted ad interim relief to PPL and restrained the nightclub owners from publicly performing or using sound recordings from PPL's repertoire without obtaining the required non-exclusive public performance licence.

Adding to this, The case came to light after a PPL representative visited Ballr on June 24 and allegedly found several popular songs being played at the venue. The tracks included ‘ Badtameez Dil ’, ‘ Mauja Hi Mauja ’, ‘ Dard-e-Disco ’, ‘ O Saki Saki ’, ‘ Dus Bahane ’, Justin Bieber's ‘ What Do You Mean ’ and Dua Lipa's ‘ Levitating ’. According to PPL, the copyrights to these recordings are held by the organisation.

Meanwhile, During the hearing, the court was informed that Ballr had previously obtained a licence to use music from PPL's repertoire. However, the licence had expired and was not renewed. Taking note of this, the court restrained the defendants from using PPL's copyrighted recordings without securing the necessary licence.

Notably, PPL has maintained that venues using copyrighted music for public entertainment must obtain the appropriate permissions. Following the court's order, PPL advocate Hiten Wasan shared the organisation would continue to identify instances of unauthorised music use and take legal action where necessary.

As per the latest buzz, He asserted, "The ad interim injunction granted by the Bombay High Court sends a clear message that continued unauthorised use of copyrighted music can have serious legal consequences."
In further updates, The order comes as PPL continues its efforts to ensure that copyrighted music is used in commercial establishments only after the required licences have been obtained.

title: Lok Sabha passes bill restricting states’ power to tax minerals amid protests
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

The Lok Sabha on Wednesday passed the Mines and Minerals (development and regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026, which aims to restrict state governments from imposing taxes, cesses or levies on minerals rights and ‘mineral-bearing lands’, via voice vote sans debate amid opposition protests.

Adding to this, The bill was passed amid opposition protests. (Sansad TV/ANI Video Grab) The bill, which amends the Mines and Minerals (development and regulation) Act, 1957, was introduced on Monday by minister of coal and mines G Kishan Reddy. It was passed in the second half of the Lok Sabha session on Wednesday, with Jagdambika Pal, who was in the chair, beginning proceedings by asking the Opposition to maintain decorum.

Meanwhile, The amendment bill introduces a new section that says that “no tax, cess or such other levy (by whatever name called) shall be imposed by the state Government on mineral rights; or mineral bearing lands, either based on mineral quantity or mineral value or royalty payable…except in accordance with such conditions or restrictions as may be prescribed by the Central Government..”

Notably, The bill also proposes to expand the central government’s powers to regulate mines to mineral bearing lands having ore content in accordance with the parameters prescribed under the MMDR Act.

As per the latest buzz, The proposed amendments are the fallout of a July 2024 ruling by the Supreme Court that upheld the power of states to levy taxes on mineral rights and and mineral-bearing lands.

In further updates, The bill clarifies any tax, cess or other levy which is not deposited with the state government or recovered by it before the commencement of the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Amendment Act, 2026, will be deemed to be invalid at all material times. However, those already deposited, will not be liable to be refunded.
On top of that, PMK chief Anbumani Ramadoss urged the Centre to immediately withdraw the proposed amendment bill, warning that it usurps the taxation rights of state governments.

title: SC to test legality of Delhi Police use of facial recognition of protesters
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

The Supreme Court on Thursday agreed to examine whether the Delhi Police’s use of facial recognition technology and biometric surveillance to monitor protesters at Jantar Mantar has legal backing, and whether such mass surveillance violates fundamental rights to privacy, dignity, free speech and peaceful assembly.

Adding to this, The plea has also sought directions to private vendors to permanently delete biometric information collected. (File photo) A bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana issued notice to the Centre and the Delhi Police commissioner on a public interest litigation filed by CPI(M) Rajya Sabha MP AA Rahim, challenging the alleged use of facial recognition technology, AI-powered surveillance systems and biometric identification tools against protesters.

Meanwhile, Senior advocate Menaka Guruswamy, appearing for Rahim, told the bench that the petition specifically challenged the use of facial recognition technology by the Delhi Police against protesters and alleged that the data collected was being held by private companies. “This is very specific prayer concerning facial recognition being used by the Delhi Police against protesters, and the data is held with private companies,” Guruswamy shared.

Notably, She shared that the surveillance involved both a facial recognition vehicle and smart glasses, with data collected without the permission of those being monitored. “One maps your face and one is a vehicle. So spectacles are used and a vehicle is also used. And that data is all taken without permission. These private entities host the data. In violation, we will argue, of the DPDP Rules, CrPC and a variety of things,” she shared.

As per the latest buzz, The bench then directed that notice be issued and the plea be tagged with other pending petitions concerning the July 20 “Sansad Chalo” protest, which raise allegations of police excesses, including the use of pellet guns and violence against protesters and police personnel.

In further updates, The petition, filed through advocate Subhash Chandran KR, claims that since the commencement of the sit-in at Jantar Mantar on June 20, thousands of protesters, journalists and ordinary citizens have been subjected to “continuous and pervasive biometric surveillance”.

On top of that, Rahim has sought a declaration that indiscriminate deployment of facial recognition and biometric surveillance against peaceful protesters is unconstitutional. He has also sought directions restraining the Delhi Police from deploying such technologies until Parliament enacts a law specifically authorising their use.

Among other reliefs, the petition seeks disclosure of the surveillance technologies, databases, standard operating procedures and vendor agreements used during the Jantar Mantar protest; deletion of protesters’ biometric data from NAFIS, CCTNS and allied databases; and a mechanism enabling individuals to ascertain whether their biometric information was collected and seek its deletion.

title: ‘Pakistan ke prem mein mare rahte hain’: Kangana Ranaut defends calling Naseeruddin Shah ‘lomdi’
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Star and BJP MP Kangana Ranaut of late took a sharp jibe at veteran star Naseeruddin Shah over his comments on student protests, referring to him as a “lomdi” (fox). Now, Kangana has defended her remark and hit out at the star over what she described as his “love for Pakistan”, while also accusing the movie industry of “hypocrisy”.

Adding to this, BJP MP Kangana Ranaut calls out movie industry's hypocrisy. (PTI Photo/Shahbaz Khan)(PTI07_21_2026_000081B) (PTI) Kangana Ranaut defends calling Naseeruddin Shah ‘lomdi’ In a conversation with ANI, Kangana criticised what she described as the movie industry’s “consistent attitude”, recalling the unrest surrounding protests at Jantar Mantar. She claimed that during the protests, several of her parliamentarian friends had people climbing onto their cars and breaking their windows, while around 2,500 people had gathered outside her home, prompting a heavy police presence that kept her family awake at night.

Meanwhile, She added, “So when a situation like this was unfolding at Jantar Mantar, they were all shedding crocodile tears. But now that children in Jharkhand are facing this kind of oppression, aren’t they Gen Z too? Is someone only considered Gen Z if they act against the country or abuse the Prime Minister? They themselves have been made to appear anti-youth. This hypocrisy in the movie industry will not work. The crocodile tears that people from the movie industry were shedding for Jantar Mantar, they should shed the same tears for the children in Jharkhand as well.”

Notably, She then defended her “lomdi” remark about Naseeruddin Shah, saying, “I shared this about Naseeruddin Shah because he had made such a distasteful video in which he was making threats of this kind. And whenever you look at his films, interviews or statements, it is always about Pakistan. Yeh Pakistan ki prem katha kab khatam hogi? Jab dekho Pakistan ke prem mein yeh mare rahte hain. Ab Partition ko bhi itne saal ho gaye hain toh yeh love story khatam kyun nahi ho rahi hai (When will this love story with Pakistan end? He is always obsessed with his love for Pakistan. So many years have passed since Partition, so why hasn’t this love story ended yet?).”

As per the latest buzz, Last week, taking to her Instagram Stories, Kangana reposted a comment by star Piyush Mishra on Naseeruddin’s remarks, in which he questioned the veteran star’s silence on the student protests in Jharkhand. She added a separate note that read, “Sach toh ye hai ki har koi kisi na kisi ka kutta hai lekin mujhe iss baat ka garv hai ki main jiss ghar (desh) ki roti khati hoon uski rakhwaali karti hoon, uske liye ladti hoon. Naseer saab khate toh iss desh ke hain lekin ladte padosi desh ke liye hai (The truth is that each and everyone of us is someone’s pet. I am proud that I protect and defend the same house from where I get my food. But Naseer saab eats from this land and defends the neighbouring country).”

title: Shriya Saran says she wasn’t invited to award shows despite nominations after Awarapan's failure: ‘I was disheartened’
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Filmmaker Mohit Suri ’s 2007 movie Awarapan, starring Emraan Hashmi , Shriya Saran and Mrinalini Sharma, underperformed at the ticket-window upon rollout but eventually developed a cult following. Now, almost two decades later, its sequel is set to hit theatres. In an interview with Pinkvilla, Shriya recalled being disheartened by the movie’s initial ticket-window performance and opened up that she was not even invited to some award shows despite the movie receiving nominations.

Adding to this, Shriya Saran recalls being disheartened after Awarapan flopped. Shriya Saran on Awarapan's failure Shriya shared, “When the movie came out, we all had lots of hopes for it. But I don’t know why; I think it was ahead of its time. It was even nominated in some award shows, and they didn’t send me an invite. It was like that. And Awarapan is a movie which I felt would be celebrated; people would love it. So when something like that happens, you kind of feel very disheartened.”

Meanwhile, The star also reflected on the movie’s enduring popularity, noting that audiences continued to tell her how much they loved it despite its initial ticket-window performance. She added, “So then, for the longest time, I thought maybe it was the songs they loved, because the songs were amazing and Emraan was amazing. But now, you know, I feel like people loved the story. They kind of felt it. Because it’s a very intense, intense story. So people really felt it. Otherwise, the amount of love they’re still giving it, the amount they’re giving to it even now, it wouldn’t be like that. It wouldn’t be.”

Notably, Awarapan is a 2007 Hindi romantic action drama directed by Mohit Suri and produced by Mahesh Bhatt and Mukesh Bhatt. Starring Emraan Hashmi, Mrinalini Sharma and Shriya Saran, the movie follows Shivam Pandit, a troubled gangster whose life begins to change when he is asked to keep watch over a Pakistani woman, Aaliyah. Although Awarapan did not perform strongly at the ticket-window upon rollout, it developed a loyal following over the years. Its music, particularly songs such as Toh Phir Aao, Tera Mera Rishta and Mahiya, became popular and contributed to the movie’s lasting appeal.

As per the latest buzz, Almost two decades later, the movie’s sequel is set to rollout in theatres. Directed by Nitin Kakkar, Awarapan 2 stars Emraan Hashmi, Disha Patani and Shabana Azmi in lead roles. The movie is scheduled to rollout in theatres on August 14 and will clash with Sunny Deol’s Batwara 1947.

title: Exclusive | Suvinder Vicky recalls abusing Arjun Rampal in Dhurandhar 2: ‘Will not go to mothers, sisters’
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

The audience took notice of Suvinder Vicky after he played the unforgettable character of policeman Balbir Singh in Kohrra . Since then, he has taken on some challenging character roles across films and web series. However, his recent projects, Satluj and Dhurandhar 2 , have placed him in two very different cinematic worlds, with the former facing a rollout ban and the latter emerging as a major smash hit.

Adding to this, Suvinder Vicky and Arjun Rampal in stills from Dhurandhar 2. In an exclusive conversation with Hindustan Times, Suvinder opened up about his contrasting roles, the depiction of violence on screen, and the responsibility of actors and filmmakers while portraying sensitive events.

Meanwhile, I am lucky that I got to star in both films. Even though my character was small and I had to abuse a lot in Dhurandhar 2, but people showered me with a lot of love. I never became a meme before, but after Dhurandhar, a lot of memes were made on my character, so I was on a high.

Notably, I am playing a negative character in Satluj, and I thought that after people see me in the movie, mujhe bahut galiyan padegi (Audience will abuse me), but those who have seen that era understand it.

As per the latest buzz, Many people might question why I do characters like this, but today's audience is smart, and they can differentiate between reel and real. But if actors did not play these characters as authentically as possible, many would not feel the fear of that time. Even if I talk about my kids, they don’t know what happened in 1984, and they don’t know who Jaswant Kalra was. So, maybe it is us actors and directors who are responsible for showing it as authentically as possible.

In further updates, We are hearing that the movie's pirated version is available. We don't support piracy, but a movie reaches the audience some way or the other. Definitely, if this movie was rolled out on 70 MM, the makers would have got their return on investment, and it would be nice to watch it on the big screen.

On top of that, There are films which are based on real life and then there are fictional films, but they are also inspired by what goes on in the society. Hum hi insaan hai, hum hi shaitan hai. It depends who takes what in what sense. It depends on your thinking and also it is your choice. Now we have options. Earlier, we only had theatres and Doordarshan. Now, we are moving with entertainment in our hands, if we don’t like something, we can go to something else. Also, it looks real on screen because everybody has done justice to their work in the movie.

I’m lucky to work with great directors. In this, the credit goes to Aditya Dhar and to me also because I also gave my hundred percent effort. Also, galiyon ka shrey hamare script writer ko bhi jayega (The credit for all the abusive language would also go our screenwriter), because I didn’t make any of those, that was all written in the script.

title: ‘Cockroaches emerge from gutters, what is wrong with that?’: Kangana Ranaut defends her gutter generation remark
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Star and BJP MP Kangana Ranaut stirred row after she shared that some young Hindu women flaunt freedom without accountability and called them ‘ generation gutter ’. After backlash over her comments, Kangana has now clarified on her comments to news agency ANI.

Adding to this, BJP MP Kangana Ranaut at the Parliament Premises during the Monsoon Session. (ANI Photo/Rahul Singh) (Rahul Singh) What Kangana shared Kangana shared she had not made a blanket statement about the protest at Jantar Mantar over the NEET-UG paper leak and she "specifically referred to some people or some women".

Meanwhile, "Those who call themselves cockroaches, and we say that cockroaches emerge from gutters, what is wrong with that? My point is simply this: if people label themselves as cockroaches, and we say the gutter is their home, why should they be offended? I certainly don't consider myself a cockroach. If someone were to say I live in a gutter, I would deny it. But if someone claims to be a cockroach, then naturally, they would live in a gutter. Where else? But to claim that I was referring to all youth is simply not the case," she shared.

Notably, "If some young people use drugs, or if we discuss the current trend of addiction involving drugs, betting, gambling, or the dark web, addressing a specific segment of the youth doesn't mean I was making a blanket statement about everyone. Did I say that all youth belong to the gutter? I specifically referred to some people or some women. So, how else should we address this?" she asked.

As per the latest buzz, Earlier, Kangana had criticized the Gen Z protests. Kangana wrote, "Never in my life have I seen so much ugliness in one place. These reels from Gen Z protests are puke-inducing. The way they speak and the kind of language they are using... never in my life have I seen everything in each and every frame so jarring and so crass all at once....I call them Generation Gutter. Some of them have nothing to offer to the system. They are not good at studies...," she had shared.

In further updates, “You call yourself cockroaches and look/behave like them as well... there is no paradox or juxtaposition there, just simply subjecting the world to your filth, garbage and ugliness. I am scarred from these reels, need some healing, digital detox,” the star had shared. Her remarks came after Delhi Police directed multiple social media platforms to remove posts and videos containing offensive and abusive remarks. The posts were allegedly uploaded during the student protests at Jantar Mantar after the police crackdown during the July 20 Chalo Sansad march.

On top of that, On the work front, Kangana Ranaut was last seen in the movie Bharat Bhhagya Viddhaata . Directed by Manoj Tapadia, the movie was based on the true story of the nurses and staff at Cama Hospital who saved the lives of patients during the 2008 Mumbai terrorist attacks. It will stream on Zee5 from August 14.

title: Anup Soni REACTS to Ajay Devgn replacing him as Crime Patrol host: “I am sure he will bring his own style and perspective”
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:
Anup Soni reacts to Ajay Devgn replacing him as Crime Patrol host, saying he is a fan of the star and wishing the new season’s team well.

Adding to this, In conversation with Variety India, Soni shared he remains grateful for his association with the franchise and the response he received from viewers over the years. “I don’t have much to say on this. I have had a long and very special association with Crime Patrol, and I am grateful for all the love and affection the audience has given me over the years,” he shared.

Notably, Devgn's entry marks a significant change for the franchise as the soon-to-release season, titled Crime Patrol 2026: Crime Ka Current Season, is set to return with a revamped presentation. The star has already shot 15 episodes of the new season, which is scheduled to premiere on August 31.

I am sure he will bring his own style and perspective to the show. I wish the team all the very best for the new season,” he shared.
